decisions.title: Retention periods by data category
decisions.decision_required: How long each category of record is kept — customer records, shipment records, package and leg history, public tracking events, consent records, audit log entries, imported files, exported files, backups — and whether automatic deletion runs at all.
decisions.affected_feature: Retention and deletion across every table; the audit log; backup rotation in docs/BACKUP_RESTORE.md.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: RC-UAT-21 (DEC-0233): the retention-deletion machinery is built -- per-class policies (period, action), a global switch, a dry-run report and a worker run only by hand -- and ships DISABLED: every class off with no period, the global switch off. Periods remain undecided; enabling needs Ben's approval (stand-ins D-6 to D-11).
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep automatic deletion disabled. Deleting on a guessed period destroys records that cannot be recovered; keeping them is reversible.
options: Per-category periods with automatic deletion once each period elapses.
One organization-wide period with automatic deletion.
Manual deletion only, on request, with no scheduled job.
No deletion at all, retaining everything indefinitely (the current behaviour), recorded as a deliberate choice rather than an omission.

consequences.security: Indefinite retention enlarges what a breach would expose. A retention job, once built, is itself destructive and needs its own authorisation and audit trail.
consequences.privacy: Keeping personal data longer than a stated purpose requires is the privacy risk here; no retention statement can be published to customers until this is answered.
consequences.operational: Database and backup size grow without bound. Restore-rehearsal timings in docs/BACKUP_RESTORE.md were measured at development size and will drift.
consequences.user_experience: None today. Once deletion runs, staff will see records disappear, so the rule must be visible in the interface before it takes effect.

decisions.provisional_uat_disposition: Retention deletion remains disabled for RC-UAT. Authorised temporary disposition; not an answer and not production approval.
decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject. RC_UAT_1_BASELINE.md section 3: 'Retention deletion | disabled | OD-01 - open'. PROJECT_STATUS.md section 9: 'Retention periods | How long each record class is kept | Any retention deletion (still not built)'.

decisions.title: Final Operations permissions
decisions.decision_required: The final permission set for the Operations role, specifically whether Operations may bulk-import a customer list, bulk-export shipments and reports, and whether any financial visibility is granted.
decisions.affected_feature: The role/permission map in backend/app/core/permissions.py; the import and export controls on the customer and shipment screens; report availability.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Operations cannot import and cannot bulk-export customers, shipments or reports (Admin-only placeholder, DEC-0082). Operations holds tariff:read (DEC-0172, OD-45), so it sees vendor cost in the Workspace and in Finance -> Payables and Profitability; only financial_cost:read (carrier cost) stays Admin's. Since OD-69 Operations also holds financial:adjust (refund, void, reopen). UAT-OP-10 pins the carrier-cost exclusion.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep the Admin-only placeholder. Granting a permission is reversible only after it has already been exercised; withholding it is not destructive.
options: Leave Operations without import or bulk export (the current placeholder).
Grant Operations bulk export of shipments but not import.
Grant Operations both import and bulk export.
Grant a narrower export limited to the shipments they own.

consequences.security: Bulk export is the widest data-egress path in the application. Widening it widens what one compromised staff session can remove.
consequences.privacy: An exported CSV leaves the application's access controls entirely. Every additional role that can export is another copy of customer data outside it.
consequences.operational: Today only an Admin can run a bulk import or export, so those tasks queue behind one role. That is a real operational cost of the placeholder.
consequences.user_experience: Operations staff see no import or export control at all — absent, not disabled — so nothing appears broken.

decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject. PROJECT_STATUS.md section 9: 'Final Operations and Marketing permissions for import and export | Who may bulk-import a customer list; who may bulk-export shipments and reports | Nothing today — Admin-only is the safe placeholder (DEC-0082)'.

decisions.title: Tracking domain
decisions.decision_required: The real public hostname and path at which customers track a shipment, and whether it is a subdomain of the company domain or a separate domain.
decisions.affected_feature: TRACKING_BASE_URL; every public tracking link printed on a label, shown in the staff interface, or placed in a customer-facing message.

decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep the development value in the UAT environment and keep the startup warning loud. A guessed production hostname would be printed onto labels.

A dedicated tracking domain.
A path on the main site.

consequences.user_experience: A customer who mistypes or cannot reach the tracking host has no other route to their shipment status.

decisions.decision_required: Which hosting providers are on the shortlist, and which one the application will actually run on.

A virtual private server the business administers.
On-premises hardware.
A Canadian-region managed host, if OD-11 requires residency.

decisions.title: Recovery point objective
decisions.decision_required: How much recorded work the business accepts losing in a failure — the maximum acceptable age of the most recent usable backup.
decisions.affected_feature: Backup frequency in docs/BACKUP_RESTORE.md section 2; scripts/backup_db.py scheduling; the hosting tier chosen under OD-10.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: No backup schedule runs. docs/BACKUP_RESTORE.md section 6 records a target of up to 1 hour during business hours and up to 12 hours overnight, and marks it explicitly as 'Target, not measured. No schedule runs today'.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep the recommended schedule documented and unclaimed. A stated RPO that no schedule delivers is worse than an admitted absence.
options: Near-zero, requiring continuous replication.
One hour during business hours.
One business day.
Best-effort, with no commitment.

consequences.security: A backup taken more often is another copy of the whole dataset, each of which needs the same protection as the live database.
consequences.privacy: Every backup copy is a copy of personal data, and its retention is bounded by OD-01.
consequences.operational: This is the decision that sets backup frequency and therefore cost. Until it is answered no schedule can be justified, so none runs.
consequences.user_experience: After a failure, the RPO is what a customer-service agent has to explain: the work that has to be re-entered.

decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject. BACKUP_RESTORE.md section 6: 'RPO — data at risk between backups | Up to 1 hour during business hours, up to 12 hours overnight... Target, not measured. No schedule runs today'. HOSTING.md section 9: 'RPO and RTO | Owner | Backup frequency and the hosting tier'.

decisions.title: Recovery time objective
decisions.decision_required: How long the business accepts being without the application after a failure, end to end, including detection and the decision to restore.
decisions.affected_feature: The restore runbook in docs/RUNBOOKS.md; scripts/restore_rehearsal.py; the hosting tier and any standby arrangement chosen under OD-10.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Restore and verification were measured at under 1 second against a 0.89 MiB development database on a local SSD. docs/BACKUP_RESTORE.md section 6 records the measurement and states plainly that it is the database step only and is misleading on its own.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep publishing the measured figure with its stated scope, and claim no end-to-end RTO.
options: Minutes, requiring a warm standby.
A few hours, achievable from a stored backup.
One business day.
Best-effort, with no commitment.

consequences.security: A shorter RTO usually means a standby copy of the database, which is another system to secure.
consequences.privacy: A standby is another live copy of personal data.
consequences.operational: This sets whether a standby is provisioned at all, and how the restore runbook is rehearsed. The measured sub-second figure will not survive production data volume.
consequences.user_experience: During an outage staff have no fallback: bookings cannot be recorded and public tracking is unavailable.

decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject. BACKUP_RESTORE.md section 6: 'RTO — time to restore service | Restore and verification measured at under 1 second at 0.89 MiB | Measured, and misleading on its own'.

decisions.title: Import file and row limits
decisions.decision_required: Whether the 2 MiB file limit and 5,000-row limit on customer CSV import match the real customer list the business intends to import.
decisions.affected_feature: MAX_FILE_BYTES and MAX_ROWS in backend/app/services/csv_safety.py; the customer import screen; the refusal message an operator sees.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: A file over 2 MiB is refused before parsing, and a file over 5,000 rows is refused after parsing, each with a message naming the limit and telling the operator to split the file. The limits are also published on the import screen.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep the limits. They bound memory and parsing time, and a refusal that names the limit is recoverable by splitting the file.
options: Keep 2 MiB and 5,000 rows.
Raise both to fit the real list in one file.
Keep the limits and document a split procedure for a larger list.
Add a background import for large files.

consequences.security: The limits are a denial-of-service bound as much as a usability one: they cap what a single upload can make the server do.
consequences.privacy: A larger import is a larger quantity of personal data arriving in one action, and the duplicate-review step scales with it.
consequences.operational: If the real list exceeds 5,000 rows, the first production import fails until somebody splits it — discovered at the worst moment unless answered first.
consequences.user_experience: The operator sees a clear refusal naming the limit rather than a timeout, so the failure is at least legible.

decisions.title: MFA requirement and implementation approach
decisions.decision_required: Whether multi-factor authentication is required for staff sign-in before production, for which roles, and by what method.
decisions.affected_feature: Staff authentication and session handling; the sign-in screen; the security section of UAT sign-off.

options: No MFA.
TOTP authenticator application for all staff.
TOTP for Admin only.
Email one-time codes.
An external identity provider carrying MFA.

consequences.operational: MFA adds enrolment, recovery and lost-device handling, none of which exists. Adding it later means re-running every authentication and session UAT case.
consequences.user_experience: Sign-in gains a step for every staff member, every session.

Purchase named hardware and test against it.
Accept on-screen and PDF rendering only, with physical acceptance deferred.

consequences.privacy: A printed label carries a recipient name and address into the physical world, where this application's controls end.
consequences.operational: Barcode density, label size and printer DPI interact. A barcode that renders correctly on screen can be unscannable at 4×6 on 203 dpi stock, and that is only discoverable with the real hardware.
consequences.user_experience: Operations staff scan packages as their main interaction. If the scanner cannot read the barcode, the workflow does not exist for them.

decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject. REVIEW_physical_label.md: 'Owner decision: OD-18 - open. The acceptance hardware has not been named.' No label has been printed or scanned.

decisions.title: Screen-reader and zoom testing responsibility
decisions.decision_required: Who runs a screen reader, zoom and forced-colors testing against the application, and what constitutes acceptance.
decisions.affected_feature: Every staff and public screen, as experienced through assistive technology.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: An automated axe audit runs over both staff and public screens at two viewports and passes with no serious or critical violation. No screen reader has ever been run against the application, no zoom level above 100% has been tested, and forced-colors mode has not been exercised. Only Chromium has been used.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep the automated result and keep it labelled as automated. Never present an axe pass as human validation.
options: A staff member who uses a screen reader daily performs it.
An external accessibility specialist performs it.
A staff member performs it after training, with the limitation recorded.
Defer, and record the application as not validated for assistive technology.

consequences.operational: Automated auditing covers roughly a third of WCAG. Announcement quality, focus order and dialog focus trapping are exactly what it cannot see, and exactly what decides whether the application is usable.
consequences.user_experience: This is the decision. Without it there is no evidence any disabled person can use this application, and no claim to that effect may be made.

decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject. REVIEW_accessibility.md: 'Owner decision: OD-19 - open. Nobody has been assigned to perform this.' Automated axe results are not human validation, and the sheet says so at the top.

decisions.title: Who may authorize production deployment
decisions.decision_required: Who is authorised to perform a production deployment, and what gate must be satisfied before they may.
decisions.affected_feature: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md; the deployment artefacts under deploy/; the release gate between a UAT candidate and production.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Production deployment is prohibited. No production environment exists, no production credential exists, and the UAT environment refuses to operate against a production database or a production account.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep deployment prohibited. An unauthorised deployment is the one action in this project that cannot be reversed by editing a file.
options: The owner alone authorises each deployment.
A named technical operator, under an owner-signed gate.
Two-person authorisation.

consequences.security: A deployment performed without a gate could publish an application whose security decisions — OD-17 above all — are still unanswered.
consequences.privacy: Going live is the moment real customer data enters the system. It must not happen before OD-01 and OD-11 are settled.
consequences.operational: Nobody currently knows who would press the button, so no deployment rehearsal can be scheduled or assigned.
consequences.user_experience: None until launch.

decisions.provisional_uat_disposition: Production deployment remains prohibited. Authorised temporary disposition; not an answer.
decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject. RC_UAT_1_BASELINE.md: 'Production deployment remains prohibited (OD-20: nobody is yet authorised to perform one).'

decisions.title: ShipStation account facts: the nine integration questions
decisions.decision_required: The nine questions in docs/INTEGRATIONS.md section 9, answered against current official documentation and against the real ShipStation account. They are reproduced verbatim in provider_questions below and are NOT answered here.
decisions.affected_feature: The provider integration seam: the adapter registry, the resource host and path-prefix allowlists, webhook ingestion, the connected_api tracking mode, and the two reserved public freshness fields.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Infrastructure only, and deliberately inert. PRODUCTION_ADAPTERS is empty; both integration resource allowlists are empty so no external request can be constructed; integration health reads not_configured; no provider webhook route exists; connected_api is refused by the tracking vocabulary and by leg_service; the public contract is 24 fields with no freshness field present.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep every allowlist empty, keep the adapter registry empty, and keep connected_api refused. An adapter written against a guessed API generation or a guessed event vocabulary would publish wrong statuses to customers.
options: Answer all nine against the real account and build the matching adapter.
Answer them and discover the account cannot support the integration, settling it as out of scope.
Continue with manual and external-link tracking only and defer indefinitely.

consequences.security: Question 5 is a security question: if webhook payloads carry no verifiable signature, every notification must stay unsigned_untrusted and only an authenticated read may move a parcel. Question 8 decides the allowlist, which is the only thing preventing an outbound fetch to an arbitrary host.
consequences.privacy: A provider integration sends shipment references to a third party and receives tracking detail back, which changes what a stranger can see on the public page.
consequences.operational: Question 4 decides the status map. Legacy SHIP_NOTIFY means a label was created, not a scan or a delivery; mapping it as delivery would publish a false delivery to a customer.
consequences.user_experience: Question 3 decides whether the interface can offer provider tracking at all or must show the limitation and fall back to external-link or manual mode.

decisions.provisional_uat_disposition: Provider resource host and path allowlists remain empty, the production adapter registry remains empty, and connected_api remains refused. Authorised temporary disposition; not an answer.
decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject, and the identifier the earlier reconstruction guessed at without assigning. The nine questions are docs/INTEGRATIONS.md section 9, deferred by DEC-0075 and tracked in PROJECT_STATUS.md section 9 as 'ShipStation product, auth, events, signatures, hosts | The nine questions in docs/INTEGRATIONS.md section 9 | The final provider phase'.
provider_questions: Which ShipStation product and API generation is the account entitled to — legacy, V2, or ShipStation API / ShipEngine?
What is the authentication scheme for that specific product?
Can the account track a label it did not purchase?
Which webhook event types exist, and what does each actually mean?
Do webhook payloads carry a verifiable signature, and by what algorithm?
Does the provider supply a stable event identifier?
What are the documented rate limits, and does the provider send Retry-After?
Exactly which HTTPS hosts and path prefixes would a resource_url fetch need?
What is the carrier coverage for VCA, CAV, CAD, and XUS?

decisions.title: Return shipment workflow and policy
decisions.decision_required: Whether return shipment records are in scope, and if so how one is created, identified, related to its outbound, routed, labelled, tracked, priced and reported. The twelve questions are reproduced in return_questions below and are NOT answered here.
decisions.affected_feature: shipments.is_return and shipments.return_of_shipment_id; the returns row in the shipment-status report; the is_return column in the shipment export; activity_service.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Both columns exist and are read by report_service, export_service and activity_service. Nothing writes either one — no service, no route, no schema field, no screen. The returns report row can only ever read 0 and the export column can only ever read false. As of RC-UAT-3 the returns row carries no drill-through link. Return statuses — return_in_progress and returned — are fully implemented, staff-recordable, and are not part of this decision.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Build nothing, manufacture no return row in any dataset, and remove the one control that promised a return-shipment list. Keep the truthful zero and keep the counting rule the fixture tests pin.
options: Returns are out of current scope; the reporting and export surfaces are reconsidered rather than left reading zero.
A return is a booking action creating a new linked shipment.
A return is an administrative correction on the outbound shipment.
Returns are tracked outside this application entirely.

consequences.security: A return workflow is a new write path against confirmed shipments and needs its own permission and audit treatment.
consequences.privacy: Question 8 decides whether a return is publicly trackable and what the customer sees on the original reference once a return exists — a public-disclosure question, not an internal one.
consequences.operational: CRM.md section 4 states returns do not count as another outbound purchase. That rule is pinned by fixture-level report and export tests and holds whether or not a workflow is ever built.
consequences.user_experience: Staff can already record that a shipment is being returned, using the two statuses. What they cannot do is create a linked return shipment, and nothing in the interface now suggests they can.

decisions.basis: Owner-supplied subject, raised by the pre-UAT gate review on 2026-09-15. blocks_local_uat is false because docs/UAT/UAT_CASES.md states that no case in the 45-case pack depends on a return record, and because the dead returns_only control was removed in RC-UAT-3. It remains open and unanswered.
return_questions: Are returns in current scope at all? If no, the reporting and export surfaces must be reconsidered rather than left reading zero.
Who may create one? Which roles — and is it a booking action, a shipment action, or an admin correction?
Does a return receive a new Solaris ID, reuse the outbound ID, or carry a derived suffix?
What relationship to the outbound shipment is required? Must return_of_shipment_id always be set, must the outbound be confirmed, must it be delivered, and may one outbound have several returns?
Package selection. All packages, a subset, or new package records? What happens to the outbound's delivered counts?
Route direction. Is a return the reverse route group, the same one, or a separately chosen route?
Label behaviour. Does a return get a printed label, and if so whose address is the recipient?
Public tracking. Is a return publicly trackable, under which reference, and what does the customer see on the original reference once a return exists?
Financial treatment. Is a return charged, free, or a refund against the outbound? How does it interact with payment_state and refund_amount?
Cancellation and rebooking interaction. May a return be cancelled? May a cancelled outbound have a return? Does a rebooking inherit its predecessor's returns?

Reporting treatment. Confirm the current rule — excluded from qualifying counts, reported on their own row — and decide whether the returns report row should link anywhere. As of RC-UAT-3 it links nowhere, because every available destination would answer question 1 by implementation.
Must legacy or imported returns be supported? Shipment import is itself unanswered (OD-15), so a return arriving from a migration has no path either.

decisions.title: Customer Account registration mode
decisions.decision_required: How a customer obtains an account, and what registration may create.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed Customer Account registration; docs/customer_account/STATE_MACHINES.md.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built (Phases 9-12, checked against the code 2026-10-21): POST /api/v1/account/register creates a pending customer identity and a pending customer-data proposal and never writes, links or merges a canonical customer; email verification uses purpose-bound, expiring, single-use tokens; Operations or Admin approve by hand in Customer accounts; an unapproved account reads no shipment; register, resend, forgot-password and sign-in answer generically. In production, registration is refused until an email provider is selected (OD-34) and approved terms and privacy versions exist (OD-37).
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Build nothing until the identity model and the approval path are specified.
options: Open registration with email verification and explicit staff approval.
Invitation-only accounts created by staff.
Open registration with automatic linking on an exact email match.

consequences.security: Automatic linking on an email match would turn control of a mailbox into control of a customer's shipment history. Staff approval is the control that stops it.
consequences.privacy: A non-generic response would confirm whether an address or a matching customer exists, which is itself a disclosure about a named person.
consequences.operational: Every registration becomes queue work for Operations. That cost is accepted deliberately in exchange for no automatic linking.
consequences.user_experience: The customer waits for approval before seeing any history, and is told so plainly.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: open registration with email verification and explicit staff approval. Registration creates a pending customer identity and a pending customer-data proposal. It must not directly create, overwrite, merge or link a canonical CRM customer. An unapproved account cannot view shipment history. Generic responses must prevent disclosure of whether an email address or matching customer exists.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Customer Account approval authority
decisions.decision_required: Who approves a customer account, and whether approval may ever be automatic.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed staff approval queue in the Staff Portal.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built: customer_account:review and customer_account:approve are held by Operations and Admin only; there is no automatic approval. Approve (create a customer or link an existing one) and reject are staff routes behind a server-calculated preview, and every approval, rejection, link and override is audited without passwords or tokens. Staff screen: Customer accounts (Customer account applications).
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: No approval mechanism at all until the authority is decided.
options: Operations approves, Admin may override.
Admin only.
Automatic approval on verified email.

consequences.security: Approval is the moment history becomes visible. An automatic rule would make a disclosure decision with no person accountable for it.
consequences.privacy: Audit payloads must carry reason codes and safe identifiers, never passwords, tokens or unnecessary customer data.
consequences.operational: Operations carries the queue; Admin can unblock it. Both actions are audited.
consequences.user_experience: Approval is not instant, and the account state says so.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: Operations performs explicit account approval. Admin may also approve as an override. No automatic approval. Approval, rejection, linking and override actions must be audited without storing passwords, tokens or unnecessary customer data in audit payloads.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Account-to-customer cardinality
decisions.decision_required: How many canonical customers one customer identity may reach, now and later.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed customer_identity_links table.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built: customer_identity_links joins an identity to a canonical customer; two partial unique indexes allow at most one active link per identity and one active link per customer in release 1, while the link table itself can carry several identities per customer later. Authorization reads the one effective link (customer_account_link_policy).
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Model nothing until the future shape is known, because the release-1 limit and the later relaxation must not require rebuilding identity ownership.
options: One identity to one customer, enforced by a nullable column on the identity.
One identity to one customer in release 1, enforced by a constraint on a separate link table that can carry many links later.
Many identities to many customers from the start.

consequences.security: A single active link per customer keeps ownership unambiguous while there is no company-access model to arbitrate between users.
consequences.privacy: One identity must never reach a second canonical customer's data.
consequences.operational: Company customers with several staff are served by one account in release 1, which Operations will have to explain.
consequences.user_experience: A company cannot yet give a colleague their own sign-in.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: one customer identity links to at most one canonical customer in release 1; the data model must support multiple identities linked to one customer later; release 1 permits only one approved active customer identity per canonical customer; no identity may access multiple canonical customers in release 1. The future limitation must not be enforced through a schema design that would make later company access require rebuilding identity ownership.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Company and multiple-user access
decisions.decision_required: Whether several people at one company may hold separate accounts in release 1.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed customer_identity_links.link_role and a later invitation model.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Nothing is implemented.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Defer the feature while keeping the relational model able to carry it.
options: Implement invitations and company administrators in release 1.
Defer, but design the relational model to support it.
Defer, and model one identity per customer with no path to more.

consequences.security: Shared access needs an authorization model — who may invite, who may revoke — that release 1 has no way to express safely.
consequences.privacy: Multi-user access means one person's action is visible to another; that needs its own decision.
consequences.operational: Companies with several shippers get one account and a manual conversation.
consequences.user_experience: No invitations, no colleague access, no shared view in release 1.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: deferred from release 1. Design the relational model to support multiple users per company/customer later, but do not implement invitations, company administrators, shared access or multi-customer access in the first release.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Customer-editable field policy
decisions.decision_required: Which customer fields a customer may submit, change directly, propose, or never see.
decisions.affected_feature: docs/customer_account/FIELD_MATRIX.md; customers, customer_addresses, consent_events, contact_suppressions.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built to the field matrix: registration accepts a fixed allowlist of fields; after approval the customer changes their preferred language directly and turns each milestone email on or off (OD-72); legal name, preferred (display) name, phone and pickup address are proposals that change nothing until Operations or Admin approve them; email is not proposable, and since RC-UAT-25 the customer cannot change the sign-in email at all: an Admin changes it from the staff account screen (Admin only, DEC-0243; the RC-UAT-21 self-service change of DEC-0231 is withdrawn) and billing address and customer type are not proposable from the account yet. Marketing consent is granted or withdrawn by the customer directly, append-only. Internal fields, financial data and suppression administration have no slot in any account response.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Expose nothing, and treat every field as invisible until it is listed.
options: Customers edit their own record directly.
Customers submit proposals that staff approve, with two low-risk exceptions.
Customers see their record but can change nothing.

consequences.security: Direct edits to identity-bearing fields would let a mailbox takeover rewrite a customer's contact details and redirect their mail.
consequences.privacy: Internal tags, notes, interactions, lifecycle status, duplicate scores and suppression administration are never customer-visible. Marketing consent is explicit, separate, unchecked by default, append-only and timestamped.
consequences.operational: Operations reviews proposed changes to identity-bearing fields.
consequences.user_experience: Two preferences apply instantly; everything else takes a review.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved with the field policy recorded in full in docs/customer_account/FIELD_MATRIX.md: a fixed registration submission list; preferred language and non-marketing operational notification preferences directly editable after approval; legal name, display name, primary contact name, email, phone, billing address, pickup/sender addresses and customer type as proposals requiring Operations approval; internal tags, lifecycle status, referral source unless explicitly collected at registration, internal notes, interactions, assigned staff, audit information, internal duplicate scores, suppression administration, financial data, staff permissions and integration state never customer-visible or customer-editable. A customer cannot remove global suppression. Marketing consent must remain explicit, separate, unchecked by default, append-only and timestamped.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Staff approval rules for customer-submitted changes
decisions.decision_required: What staff must approve, what they must see before approving, and what may merge.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed proposal-review screen in the Staff Portal; existing duplicate review.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built: a registration is reviewed with entered and normalized values and duplicate candidates from the existing duplicate_service; a post-approval change request is decided per field group by Operations or Admin, showing the proposed value, the value at submission, the value now and the normalized value; a group whose canonical value moved since submission is refused rather than merged. Preferred language and milestone-email choices apply directly. Nothing merges automatically; each decision is audited with the actor.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Approve nothing automatically and merge nothing automatically.
options: Approve every change, including preferences.
Approve identity-sensitive and canonical changes; apply two low-risk preferences directly.
Approve only name and email changes.

consequences.security: An approval screen that hides the current value invites an approver to overwrite something they never saw.
consequences.privacy: Duplicate implications are staff-facing; they must never reach a customer response.
consequences.operational: Exact and probable duplicates enter the existing review process rather than a new one built beside it.
consequences.user_experience: The customer sees the state of each proposal they submitted.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: Operations or Admin must approve every identity-sensitive or canonical customer-data change. Preferred language and operational-notification preferences may apply directly. No automatic merge. Exact and probable duplicates enter the existing review process. Approval must show the proposed value, the current value, the normalized value where relevant, duplicate implications, the affected account, the actor and the audit outcome.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Shipment ownership and history visibility
decisions.decision_required: What makes a shipment visible to an authenticated customer, and what staff must see before that visibility is granted.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed authenticated shipment list and detail; shipments.customer_id.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built: the account's shipment routes authorize only through the identity's effective link to its canonical customer, in the query itself; no email, phone, browser-supplied customer ID or tracking reference authorizes. Before approving, the reviewer sees and acknowledges the historical-shipment disclosure (count, oldest and newest dates, cancelled and rebooked included), stored with its figures; the same inclusion rule serves the account. Linked return shipments remain under OD-22.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Serve no shipment data to any account until ownership is defined server-side.
options: Authorize on the canonical customer's shipper relationship only.
Authorize on matching email or phone.
Authorize on possession of a tracking reference.

consequences.security: Email, phone and reference possession are all guessable or transferable. The shipper relationship is the only claim the CRM actually records.
consequences.privacy: Approval opens a person's whole shipping history to an account. The approver is shown the size of that disclosure before it happens.
consequences.operational: Cancelled and rebooked shipments stay visible with safe states rather than vanishing and generating support calls.
consequences.user_experience: A customer sees their own history, including the shipments that went wrong.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: shipment visibility is based only on the canonical customer's shipper relationship. Do not authorize through email, phone, browser-supplied customer ID or possession of a tracking reference. After account approval, historical qualifying shipments linked to that shipper become visible. Before approval, staff must see and explicitly acknowledge how many historical shipments will become visible, the oldest and newest shipment dates, and whether cancelled or rebooked shipments are included. Cancelled and rebooked shipments remain visible with safe states. Return event statuses remain visible where already supported; linked return-shipment records remain governed by OD-22.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Recipient access
decisions.decision_required: Whether a recipient may hold an authenticated account in release 1.
decisions.affected_feature: Public Tracking; proposed Customer Account.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Recipients use unauthenticated Public Tracking, as today.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Grant no authenticated recipient access.
options: No recipient accounts in release 1.
Recipient accounts authorized by recipient email.
Recipient accounts authorized by tracking-reference possession.

consequences.security: Recipient ownership cannot be established from data the CRM holds: a recipient email or phone is supplied by the sender and is not verified.
consequences.privacy: Inferring recipient identity would expose a shipment to whoever the sender typed.
consequences.operational: Recipients keep the Public Tracking path they already use.
consequences.user_experience: No change for recipients.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: no authenticated recipient access in release 1. Recipients continue using public tracking. Do not infer recipient ownership from recipient email, phone, address or tracking-reference possession.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Authenticated shipment field allowlist
decisions.decision_required: Which shipment fields the authenticated list and detail may contain.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed AccountShipmentListItem and AccountShipmentDetail schemas.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built: standalone account schemas declared field by field, inheriting from no staff or public schema: the list has 18 fields and the detail 25 (the 24 public-tracking fields plus booking_reference, DEC-0163). Timeline entries carry the event type and scope so the account can word them in the customer's language (Phase 15). The public 24-field contract is unchanged and pinned by its own test.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Declare a standalone allowlist and start at parity with the public contract.
options: Reuse the public tracking schema.
Reuse the staff shipment schema with fields removed.
Declare standalone schemas, starting at the same 24 values.

consequences.security: A schema that inherits another silently publishes whatever the parent gains later.
consequences.privacy: Every additional field is a separate disclosure decision about a real shipment.
consequences.operational: The public contract does not move, so Public Tracking is unaffected by Customer Account work.
consequences.user_experience: The authenticated detail shows what the customer already sees publicly, plus the ability to find it without a reference.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: release 1 uses an authenticated shipment list containing only the minimum safe list fields, and a standalone authenticated shipment-detail schema containing exactly the existing 24 public-tracking fields initially. The customer-account schema must be separately declared field by field. It must not inherit from staff shipment schemas or public tracking schemas. The public 24-field contract remains unchanged. The authenticated list may contain only safe identifiers and summary fields needed to select one of the customer's authorized shipments, and every list field and source column must be documented explicitly.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Customer financial visibility
decisions.decision_required: Whether any financial value appears on the Customer Account in release 1.
decisions.affected_feature: shipments financial columns; payment_state; declared value.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built, as narrowed by OD-77 (2026-10-20, the newer answer): the Customer Account shows no invoice, payment, balance, cost, profit, margin, exchange rate or markup on any screen or response. The only financial figures it shows are those of a quote that staff sent to the customer under OD-77 (Quotes: service, billable weight, rate per kg, base charge, the surcharges the customer pays and the total before tax, in CAD). OD-77 narrows OD-32 to that one exception; nothing else financial reaches the account.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Show no financial value at all.
options: No financial visibility in release 1.
Show invoice and balance.
Show declared value only.

consequences.security: Financial data is the highest-value target on the record and has no role in tracking a parcel.
consequences.privacy: Prices and refunds are commercially sensitive to both parties.
consequences.operational: Billing questions continue to go to staff, as today.
consequences.user_experience: The customer sees shipments, not money.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: no financial, revenue, cost, profit, invoice, balance or payment information is visible in release 1.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Customer-account multi-factor authentication
decisions.decision_required: Whether the Customer Account offers or requires MFA in the first release.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed customer identity and session model.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Nothing is implemented. Staff MFA is itself undecided (OD-17, open).
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Design so that MFA can be added, and add none yet.
options: Optional TOTP, disabled by default, in a later hardening phase.
Required MFA from release 1.
No MFA and no design provision for it.

consequences.security: A stolen customer password is sufficient for account takeover in release 1. That is an accepted residual risk, recorded in the threat model.
consequences.privacy: MFA secrets are credential material and must never appear in an audit payload.
consequences.operational: Optional MFA creates support load for lost devices; requiring it later is a separate decision.
consequences.user_experience: No second factor to set up in release 1.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: optional TOTP, disabled by default, may be designed for the later hardening phase. It is not part of the first customer-identity implementation phase. Customer MFA must remain separate from staff MFA decision OD-17. The architecture must avoid preventing required customer MFA later.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-19 lifting the CRM.md customer self-service deferral for a limited authenticated Customer Account phase. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Production email delivery
decisions.decision_required: Which provider delivers customer email in production, and what blocks launch until one is chosen.
decisions.affected_feature: Proposed email transport seam; verification, reset and account messages.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Built as answered: the account email seam has a null transport (the default) and a capture transport that writes local files and opens no socket (development and UAT only, refused in production). No production provider is written: selecting it fails at startup. Account, milestone and quote emails all go through this seam, so no email reaches anybody; production registration stays blocked until a provider is selected.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Use a development capture that opens no socket, and select nothing.
options: Select a provider now from unverified documentation.
Development-only capture; provider selection blocks production launch.
Send through a personal mailbox.

consequences.security: Credentials for a mail provider are production secrets and need a secret store.
consequences.privacy: Message content and delivery logs carry customer addresses, so data residency is an owner question, not an implementation detail.
consequences.operational: Registration cannot launch in production until delivery is real and authenticated (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) on the sending domain.
consequences.user_experience: Customers cannot register in production until this is answered.

options: Self-service hard delete.
Staff-executed, audited requests supporting deactivation, revocation, export and legally required deletion or correction.
No privacy request path at all.

consequences.security: A self-service hard delete is an irreversible destructive action reachable with one stolen password.
consequences.privacy: Deletion interacts with retention obligations that have not been established; legal review determines the applicable response period and retention exceptions.
consequences.operational: Requests become staff work with an audit trail and a reason code.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: requests are staff-executed and audited. No self-service hard-delete button. decisions.title: Linked-customer merge policy
decisions.decision_required: What a customer merge must do when the source customer, the surviving customer, or both hold an active Customer Account identity link.
decisions.affected_feature: Existing customer merge (Staff Portal, POST /api/v1/customers/merge and customer_service.merge_customers); Phase 10 Customer Account approval and linking.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Before this decision the merge service knew nothing about customer_identity_links. Merging a linked customer left the link active and pointing at the tombstoned record, which tests/test_account_activation_invariant.py recorded as a discovered limitation rather than a behaviour anybody chose. Merging into a linked surviving customer silently grew that account's disclosable shipment history.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Refuse the merge entirely while either side is linked, and change nothing else.
options: Refuse the merge while either side holds an effective link, and require explicit Customer Account reconciliation first.
Move the link to the surviving customer automatically.
Revoke the link automatically and let the merge proceed.
Suspend or deactivate the identity automatically and let the merge proceed.
Let the merge proceed and leave the link pointing at the tombstoned record.

consequences.security: Moving a link grants an identity access to a record nobody authorised it against; leaving one on a tombstone is a live grant against a record no invariant covers. Refusing grants nothing.
consequences.privacy: OD-29 requires an explicit, acknowledged disclosure of how much shipment history a link makes visible. A merge acknowledges nothing, so any option that keeps a link alive across a merge discloses history nobody previewed.
consequences.operational: Staff cannot merge duplicates involving an account holder until a reconciliation workflow exists. The refusal names which side blocked, so the record to take to reconciliation is identified.
consequences.user_experience: An account holder is never silently unlinked, suspended or deactivated because staff tidied up a duplicate record.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: a customer merge must be refused when either the source customer or the intended surviving customer has an active Customer Account identity link. The merge must not move the identity link, must not silently preserve a link on a tombstoned customer, must not expand the linked identity's shipment history, must not revoke the link automatically, must not suspend or deactivate the identity automatically, and must not treat a merge as implicit approval of a new disclosure scope. Return a safe staff-visible conflict requiring explicit Customer Account reconciliation. A future phase may implement a dedicated merge-with-account reconciliation workflow containing a fresh duplicate review, a disclosure preview, an acknowledgement, session handling and an explicit owner-approved link transition; that workflow is not part of Phase 10. The policy is necessary because moving a link may expose a different or larger shipment history, OD-29 requires explicit history-disclosure acknowledgement, the surviving customer may already have an identity, rollback and audit semantics differ among move, revoke and suspend, a tombstoned link is invalid, and refusing the merge is the safest reversible behaviour.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-20 closing the customer-merge/account-link gate left open by Phase 10. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.

decisions.title: Additional authenticated shipment-list filters
decisions.decision_required: Whether the authenticated Customer Account shipment list may offer filters beyond the status group and date range approved by OD-31 and SHIPMENT_ALLOWLISTS.md section 3.2, and if so exactly which.
decisions.affected_feature: GET /api/v1/account/shipments; backend/app/services/customer_account_shipment_service.py; the Phase 12 Customer Account shipment-list screen and its URL-addressable filter state.
decisions.current_implemented_behavior: Phase 11 implements exactly two filters, status group and booking-date range, because SHIPMENT_ALLOWLISTS.md section 3.2 approves those two and declines free-text search in release 1 in as many words. The Phase 11 instruction named a route filter and a search by the customer's own Solaris shipment reference; both were refused as unapproved and the refusal was recorded, with tests asserting their absence, in PROJECT_STATUS.md section 25.15.
decisions.safest_temporary_behavior: Keep the two approved filters and add nothing. A customer with a long history pages through it, which is slower but discloses nothing new.
options: Approve exactly two additional exact-match filters: the customer's own Solaris shipment reference, and the route group. No free text, no substring, no carrier tracking number, no package reference, no recipient field.
Approve a general free-text search box over the customer's own shipments.
Approve the reference filter only, and leave route grouping to the status filter.
Approve nothing further and keep status group and date range alone.

consequences.security: An exact-match filter over a reference the caller may already hold adds no authorization path: the ownership clause is still in the SQL and is applied before the filter, so a foreign or unknown reference narrows the caller's own rows to none rather than reaching anybody else's. A free-text option would have been different: a LIKE over a reference column turns the list into an oracle that answers prefix questions, and over any other column it would read a field the 17-field allowlist excludes.
consequences.privacy: No new field is disclosed. The reference filter matches a value the list already returns; the route group is already list field 3. Because an unknown reference and a foreign one both produce an empty list rather than a refusal, the filter cannot distinguish 'no such shipment' from 'not yours' either.
consequences.operational: A customer who has shipped many times can find one parcel without paging. Support calls that begin with a reference read off a label can be answered by the customer rather than by staff.
consequences.user_experience: Two more controls on one screen, both reflected in the URL so a filtered view is shareable and survives a refresh. An exact-match box that finds nothing for a partial reference is a wording problem, solved by labelling it as exact rather than by loosening the match.

decisions.owner_answer: Approved: exactly two additional authenticated shipment-list filters, and no others. (1) Exact Solaris shipment reference: exact match only after canonical normalization, restricted to the customer's own reference, with no substring, prefix, fuzzy or general free-text search, no carrier tracking-number search, no package-reference search, and no recipient name, email, phone or address search; bounded input; validation inside the established Customer Account error boundary rather than a framework-generated constraint response; unknown and foreign references both producing an empty list with equivalent safe behaviour; malformed input unable to bypass the account read limiter; and no ownership leak through counts, errors, headers or query order. (2) Exact route group: the validated route-group vocabulary only, no arbitrary SQL and no free-text value, invalid values answered by the established safe validation response, filtering still scoped by the effective linked customer, and no cross-customer counts. Both must compose safely with the status and date-range filters. SHIPMENT_ALLOWLISTS.md and the related requirements are to be amended before the filters are implemented, and backend tests are to land before any screen consumes them.
decisions.basis: Owner decision of 2026-09-21, issued with the Phase 12 instruction, refining the release-1 filter set that SHIPMENT_ALLOWLISTS.md section 3.2 fixed in Phase 8 and Phase 11 implemented. Recorded as an owner answer, not a recommendation.
